name: Neriah
title: Baruch's Father and Jeremiah's Scribe
summary: Neriah was the father of Baruch, who served as scribe and secretary to the prophet Jeremiah. He was also the father of Seraiah, who was a court official under King Zedekiah. Through his sons, Neriah played an indirect but important role in preserving Jeremiah's prophecies during Judah's final days before the exile.

keyEvents.title: Baruch Writes Down Jeremiah's Words
keyEvents.description: Neriah's son Baruch was called to write down all of Jeremiah's prophecies on a scroll, by the Lord's command. Baruch is consistently identified as 'son of Neriah'.

keyEvents.title: Baruch Reads the Scroll in the Temple
keyEvents.description: Baruch, son of Neriah, read Jeremiah's words aloud to all the people in the house of the Lord, causing great disturbance among the leaders.

keyEvents.title: The Scroll Is Burned by King Jehoiakim
keyEvents.description: When King Jehoiakim heard the contents of the scroll that Baruch son of Neriah had written, he cut it into pieces and burned it. But Jeremiah dictated the words again to Baruch.

keyEvents.title: Baruch Accused of Influencing Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: Neriah's son Baruch was accused by military leaders of inciting Jeremiah to warn the people against going to Egypt after the fall of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Seraiah Sent to Babylon
keyEvents.description: Neriah's other son, Seraiah son of Neriah son of Mahseiah, was sent to Babylon along with King Zedekiah. Jeremiah gave him a scroll containing prophecies against Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Comforting Words for Baruch
keyEvents.description: Jeremiah delivered a special word from the Lord to Baruch son of Neriah, in which God promised to spare his life even though judgment would come upon the land.
